coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: The Stack (Unit 3 smokestack)
record.summary: A 300-foot concrete boiler exhaust stack next to the Unit 3 Power Block (the 2018 Draft EIR dates both to 1965; press reports give 1962 for the power plant); explicitly retained as an existing structure under the Design for Development, and proposed by the developer (May 2025) as a temporary art gallery within the interim Prequel Park.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- Figure 6.2.3 marks this with a single point symbol and the label 'STACK / EXISTING STRUCTURE (~300')', not a footprint outline, but this polygon has been rebuilt 2026-09-16 (second revision) to trace the structure's actual visible footprint in satellite imagery (an earlier version read it as a fallen or lowered stack, which no source reports: the D4D, the 2018 Draft EIR and the Chronicle of May 22, 2025 all describe a standing ~300-ft Stack retained by the plan, so the polygon may instead trace the imaged lean of the standing Stack rather than its base; unconfirmed; details are in this shape's mapping log) rather than a diagram-derived placeholder. Treat as accurate to roughly 5-10m -- limited mainly by how precisely the lon/lat grid overlay could be read against the image, not by diagram-transform error. the active lots under this drawing are DataSF's active lot 4175028 (21,885 m2, 1241 Delaware St, PPS-MU zoning, recorded 2022-08-30) (253 m2 of it) and two thin roadside strips, 4232016 (614 m2, 71 m2 inside) and 4232015 (972 m2, 37 m2 inside), which are not the stack's own lots. DataSF also lists the retired lot 4232006 (38,592 m2) under it, and retired lots are not used. No active lot is the stack's own, so the drawing is kept.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final (February 26, 2020), Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: This is an existing structure without its own subdivided Assessor parcel -- it sits within the larger, largely unaddressed former power-station site. DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) shows this polygon straddling active lots 4175028 (1241 Delaware St), 4232016 and 4232015; the 2018 Draft EIR lists the Power Station sub-area as Assessor's Block 4175 Lots 002/017 and Block 4232 Lots 001/006.
notes.regulatory_context: The historic ~300 ft tall smokestack from the power station's Unit 3 generating block, called out on the D4D's own Figure 6.2.3 as 'EXISTING STRUCTURE (~300')' the plan retains (Standard 6.2.1 sets its height limit at its existing height) -- a literal, physical landmark left standing amid the redevelopment, marked on Figure 6.2.3 in the open space just south of Block 9's outlined footprint, not inside it (see the Potrero Power Station Block 9 record for that block; D4D section 4.21 treats the land around the Stack as Stack Plaza, 'the signature public space of the Power Station'), at the site's waterfront edge. The Block 9 Building Configurations inset on the same figure shows two alternate massing options labeled 'WITH UNIT 3' and 'WITHOUT UNIT 3' -- meaning the adjacent Unit 3 power block building (distinct from the Stack itself) may or may not be retained; the diagram does not draw Unit 3's own footprint distinctly enough to trace separately, so it is not mapped here as its own feature.

open_questions: The Stack's construction date differs between sources. The 2018 Draft EIR gives 1965 (Table 4.D-1, source line 'San Francisco Planning Department HRER, 2018', lists the Boiler Stack as 1965; section 4.D: 'both constructed in 1965'; project description, section 2.D.4: 'Boiler Stack (ca. 1965)'). The Chronicle (May 22, 2025) says 'a remnant of the retired power plant built in 1962' and SF YIMBY (Oct 24, 2025) says 'the retired 1962-built power plant'; neither gives the Stack's own year. The final Design for Development says PG&E added Unit 3 'in the 1960s' and captions a '1964 photo of Unit 3 and the Stack'. The DEIR says the Third Street Industrial District was documented in 2008 with a period of significance ending in 1958, and that the 2018 historic resource evaluation extended it to 1965, adding the Stack and Unit 3. This dossier gives the DEIR's date as the DEIR's and does not choose between the sources.

ICA SF's press release (Oct 28, 2025) says it will launch a public art initiative at 'The Stack at Prequel Park' in 2027, turning the Stack into 'a vertical gallery', and its exhibition page says 'Opening Fall 2027'. The Port Commission memo (Nov 14, 2025) says the Planning Department issued a temporary use authorization for Prequel Park in June 2025 and that the developer hopes to open the park in the first quarter of 2027 (page 2) or the third quarter of 2027 (page 4). No source says whether that authorization covers opening the Stack itself to visitors. The DataSF building-permit applications for Prequel Park (202512051053, 202512051066, 202512081182) were all 'filed' with no issued date in the data read on 2026-10-12, and none of their descriptions mentions the Stack.

Structural condition: the 2018 Draft EIR (Mitigation Measure M-CR-5e) says a preservation plan 'shall include stabilization of the Boiler Stack prior to construction' only 'If deemed necessary upon further condition assessment of the resource'; no condition assessment was found. Ownership: the DEIR describes the Power Station sub-area as 'currently owned by the project sponsor' but does not say which lot holds the Stack, and no source read says who owns the Stack's parcel today. Landmark status: the DEIR says the Stack is a contributor to the Third Street Industrial District and 'is not considered to be individually significant'; no source read shows an individual landmark designation.
